description: Six-panel composite figure (four different panel types) combining X-ray diffraction, EBSD mapping and TEM on Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C austenitic low-density steel. (a) XRD profile, Intensity (a.u.) versus 2θ (degree) from 30 to 100°, showing only five labelled reflections — γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311), γ(222) — i.e. single-phase FCC austenite with no second-phase peaks. (b) EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) map: many equiaxed recrystallized grains coloured by orientation, 35 μm scale bar; the right-hand keys give cubic (001/101/111) and hexagonal (0001/2-1-10/10-10) IPF colour triangles. (c) EBSD phase map of the same field: a black grain-boundary network on a uniformly red background, legend red = FCC and green = BCC, with no green (BCC) regions resolved. (d) Bright-field TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, showing dislocation tangles and elongated subgrain/band structure. (e) Dark-field TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, same condition, showing a dense uniform dispersion of bright nanometre-scale particles. (f) SAED pattern at the zone axis printed Z=[011] with FCC matrix spots labelled (111), (200), (000) and weaker spots labelled (100) and (011) — marked κ and joined by yellow lines inside a green hexagonal grid. Together the panels argue that the alloy is recrystallized single-phase FCC austenite containing nanoscale intragranular κ-carbide.

subfigures.description: XRD profile of the Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C steel: Intensity (a.u.) vs 2θ (degree) over 30-100°, with five labelled FCC austenite peaks γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311), γ(222); no other phase reflections are visible.

EBSD inverse pole figure (IPF) map of equiaxed recrystallized grains in many orientations/colours, 35 μm scale bar, with cubic (001/101/111) and hexagonal (0001/2-1-10/10-10) IPF colour triangles at the right.
EBSD phase map of the same field, uniformly red with black grain boundaries; legend gives FCC = red and BCC = green, and no green regions are visible, indicating a single FCC phase.
Bright-field TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, showing dislocation tangles, dense dislocation walls and dark elongated band/subgrain features.
Dark-field TEM micrograph, 100 nm scale bar, on the same condition, showing a dense and fairly uniform dispersion of bright nanometre-scale particles (κ-carbide) against a dark matrix.

SAED pattern with the zone axis printed as Z=[011]; matrix spots labelled (111), (200), (000) form a green hexagonal grid, while weaker spots labelled (100) and (011) are joined by yellow lines and marked κ.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an XRD pattern with 2θ (degree) on the x-axis from 30 to 100 and Intensity (a.u.) on the y-axis; only five reflections are labelled, γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311) and γ(222).
No diffraction peaks other than the labelled γ (austenite) peaks are visible in the panel (a) pattern, supporting a single-phase FCC structure.
No numeric intensity or peak-position values are printed in panel (a); intensities are given only in arbitrary units.
Panel (b) is an EBSD IPF map with a 35 μm scale bar and contains equiaxed grains of many orientations, consistent with a recrystallized microstructure.
The colour keys to the right of panels (b)/(c) show two IPF triangles, a cubic one labelled 001, 101, 111 and a hexagonal one labelled 0001, 2-1-10, 10-10.
Panel (c) is an EBSD phase map that is uniformly red with a black grain-boundary network; the legend defines red = FCC and green = BCC, and no green (BCC) regions appear.
Panel (d), a bright-field TEM micrograph with a 100 nm scale bar, shows dislocation tangles and dark elongated band-like structures within the grains.
Panel (e), a dark-field TEM micrograph with a 100 nm scale bar, shows a dense, fairly uniform dispersion of bright nanometre-scale particles, the κ-carbide precipitates.

Panel (f) is an SAED pattern with the zone axis printed as Z=[011], indexing FCC matrix spots (111), (200), (000) on a green hexagonal grid and additional weak spots (100) and (011) joined by yellow lines and labelled κ.

The caption identifies the panels as: (a) XRD profile, (b) inverse pole figure (IPF) map, (c) EBSD phase map, (d) bright field (BF) TEM micrograph, (e) dark field (DF) TEM micrograph, (f) selected area electron diffraction (SAED).
The caption states the figure reports experimental results for the Fe-30Mn-8Al-1C austenitic low-density steel.
The citing text states the measured chemical composition of the alloy is (wt.%): Mn 30.4 %, Al 7.9 %, C 1.1 %, Fe balance.
The citing text states that the microstructure is recrystallized with an average grain size of 17 μm and a single FCC phase, and that Fig. 8a reveals only FCC single-phase peaks in the XRD profile.

The citing text states that nanoscale κ phases precipitated under aging at 550 °C are confirmed by the BF and DF TEM micrographs and by selected-area diffraction, and that the κ phase forms a (γ + κ) dual phase at 500-600 °C.
